title: What triggered the Younger Dryas cold snap
summary: Scientists agree a weakened Atlantic overturning circulation caused the chill, but the trigger is unsettled; the classic meltwater-flood route faces problems and the volcanic idea is unresolved.
why: The cold snap struck just as people in West Asia began moving toward farming.
question: What triggered the sudden Younger Dryas cooling 12,900 years ago?
evidence: Cooling began about 12,870 years BP, ended about 11,700; Lake Agassiz and Mackenzie River meltwater routes proposed; no matching sea-level rise; no dated impact crater.
wouldSettle: Dated sediment evidence of a meltwater flood or a volcanic marker exactly at the onset.

theories.name: Meltwater flood
theories.idea: Glacial lake water, via Lake Agassiz or the Mackenzie River, weakened the Atlantic circulation.

theories.name: Volcanic trigger
theories.idea: An eruption started the cooling; the debate continues without conclusive proof or rejection.
